space_groups.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "32534756 ... 32 534 756": a space groups the digits.

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "Nouns following a number in the nominative singular are usually in the singular partitive case, if the noun does not need to be in any other case and if the number is any number other than yksi \"one\""; so "yksi miljoona" but "kaksi miljoonaa" (CLDR 48 RBNF fi %spellout-cardinal and its ten case rulesets (genitive, partitive, essive, translative, inessive, elative, illative, adessive, ablative, allative), ICU 78 rendering of 1000000: "yksi miljoona", "yhden miljoonan", "yhtä miljoonaa", "yhtenä miljoonana", "yhdeksi miljoonaksi", "yhdessä miljoonassa", "yhdestä miljoonasta", "yhteen miljoonaan", "yhdellä miljoonalla", "yhdeltä miljoonalta", "yhdelle miljoonalle"; CLDR 48 RBNF fi %spellout-cardinal and its ten case rulesets (genitive, partitive, essive, translative, inessive, elative, illative, adessive, ablative, allative), ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "kaksi miljoonaa", "kahden miljoonan", "kahta miljoonaa", "kahtena miljoonana", "kahdeksi miljoonaksi", "kahdessa miljoonassa", "kahdesta miljoonasta", "kahteen miljoonaan", "kahdella miljoonalla", "kahdelta miljoonalta", "kahdelle miljoonalle").

plural_scale_needs_count.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "Nouns following a number ... are usually in the singular partitive case": the partitive "tuhatta", "miljoonaa" follows a count ("kaksituhatta", "kaksi miljoonaa").

joiner_tens_units.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "3721 is kolme-tuhatta-seitsemän-sataa-kaksi-kymmentä-yksi": no conjunction joins the parts.

ordinal_style.source: Finnish ordinals are entries with "ordinal": true; a number whose last word is ordinal is ordinal. No entry has the role "ordinal".

compound_words.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "3721 is kolme-tuhatta-seitsemän-sataa-kaksi-kymmentä-yksi (actually written as one long word with no dashes in between)".

inflection_position.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish numerals" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_numerals.wikitext): "Numbers can be inflected by case; all parts of the number except toista are inflected"; "kolmellekymmenelleviidelle hengelle".

dot_ordinal.source: fi.wikipedia, "Järjestysluku" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/fiwiki-Järjestysluku.wikitext): "numeraaleja ensimmäinen, toinen, kolmas, (1., 2., 3.)": a period after the digits writes an ordinal.

joiner.source: "ja" joins a half to a number ("kaksi ja puoli"); Wiktionary, "puolitoista" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-fi-puolitoista.wikitext) glosses "puolitoista" as "one and a half". No conjunction joins the parts of a number.

decimal_marker.source: Wiktionary, "pilkku" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-fi-pilkku.wikitext): "comma; decimal point (Finnish uses a comma)".

minus_idioms.source: No Finnish idiom puts "miinus" before a positive number.

of.source: Finnish has no word that multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: Finnish puts no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: Finnish has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Finnish has no class noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Finnish puts "puoli" before the unit ("puoli kiloa"), not after the joiner.

abbreviation.source: No Finnish number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: The comma is the Finnish decimal mark (CLDR 48 fi), so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Finnish puts the word for "between" after the numbers, as a postposition with the genitive ("kahden ja viiden välillä"); no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Kielitoimiston ohjepankki writes a case ending after digits with a colon ("5:llä", "5:nä"); the ending is no number word.

fi.weak.a.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish noun cases" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_noun_cases.wikitext): genitive "-n", translative "-ksi", inessive "-ssa", elative "-sta", adessive "-lla", ablative "-lta", allative "-lle", on the weak stem with back vowels; the CLDR fi case forms of each entry show which stem takes them ("kahden", "kahdella", "kahdelle").

fi.weak.ä.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish noun cases" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_noun_cases.wikitext): the same endings with front vowels ("-ssä", "-stä", "-llä", "-ltä") after a stem with front vowels; CLDR fi: "viiden", "viidellä", "viidelle".

fi.partitive.a.source: Wikipedia, "Finnish noun cases" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Finnish_noun_cases.wikitext): partitive "-(t)a -(t)ä"; CLDR fi: "kahta", "kolmea", "sataa".
